title: Supported boundary certificates for Hilbert coefficient transforms
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field, $A=L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_r]]$, $\mathfrak m=(W,Z)$, and $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subset A$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix positive degrees $d_i$, ordered orthant vertices $(0,\alpha_i)$ of degrees $d_i$, and first-vertex quotient supports $\Delta_i$ as in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Group vertices by degree and write $Z^\ell$ for the essential variables of each accumulated block. Suppose pure transverse forms $A_i(Z)$ of degrees $d_i$ have unique supported homogeneous division for every degree prefix, and $f_i(0,Z)=A_i(Z)$ modulo terms of degree greater than $d_i$. Suppose the following certificates hold: every $Z^\beta f_i$ is a sum $\sum_hq_hf_h$ with $q_h$ supported in $\Delta_h$; the block derivatives $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)}$, with $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$, belong to $(Z^\ell)$ with invertible transverse Jacobian; and $\partial_{Z^\ell}^\delta f_i\in(Z^\ell)$ for later blocks whenever $\delta$ lies in the prefix diagram and $|\delta|\le Q$, where $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. These are identities of whole series, including all multiplication certificates, not only equalities of initial forms.
Put $D=\bigcup_i((0,\alpha_i)+\mathbf N^{m+r})$ and $H_D(t)=\#\{\eta\notin D:|\eta|\le t\}$. Write $f_i=\sum_\gamma c_{i\gamma}(W)Z^\gamma$ and $S$ for the conditions $\operatorname{ord}c_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$. Order means containment in the corresponding power of $(W)$, with infinite order for zero [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. Then $H_K(t)=\dim_L A/(K+\mathfrak m^{t+1})$ is lexicographically at most $H_D$, and equals $H_D$ exactly when $S$ holds. When $S$ holds, the $f_i$ have orders $d_i$, have supported homogeneous division for every prefix, and generate $K$ by supported sums. Moreover $K:e^\infty=K$ for every coefficient coordinate $e=W_j$, where $K:e^\infty=\{f:\exists v\ge0,\ e^vf\in K\}$. Without $S$, saturation by such an $e$ can only further decrease $H_K$, so cannot produce the level $H_D$ from a strictly smaller function. The assertions include coefficient-field extensions and empty families ($K=0,D=\varnothing$).
The conclusion applies to the regular Taylor models of such certificates after boundary-chart substitutions $W_u=e$, $W_v=e(\xi+V)$ with all $Z$ unchanged, provided the displayed pure transverse forms and whole-series certificates are retained at the point in question. It does not assert that an arbitrary equality-locus-only standard basis retains these certificates.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, route reference; detailed BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1--6.3,6.5--6.6, read online at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580; BM2 (1997), Chapter III, especially Theorems 7.14,7.20,9.6. Archival BMT and BM2 WANTED. No Stacks tag states this presentation theorem.

proof.text: Suppose $S$ holds. For $|\gamma|<d_i$, the order of $c_{i\gamma}(W)Z^\gamma$ is at least $d_i$; the other terms automatically have that order. The degree-$d_i$ part $H_i(W,Z)$ restricts at $W=0$ to $A_i(Z)$. The pure supported division hypothesis makes $A_i$ nonzero (the column with quotient $1$ belongs to its basis), so $\operatorname{ord}f_i=d_i$. Apply [lem-trf-homogeneous-division-extra-variables] with $U=W,V=Z$ to each degree prefix. It gives supported homogeneous division for the corresponding $H_i$ in all variables. Then [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] gives unique formal division, continuous quotient and remainder maps, and a closed space $M$ of supported sums, equal to the kernel of its remainder map $r$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, route reference; BM 1997, (7.2)(1)--(2), Lemma 7.3, p.263. Extra-variable specialization of the formal division calculation.

proof.text: Still under $S$, each multiplication certificate puts $Z^\beta f_i$ in $M$. Since all vertices have zero $W$ components, multiplying its quotients by a $W$-monomial preserves their supports $\Delta_h$. Thus every polynomial multiple of every $f_i$ lies in $M$. For any series $a_i$, its finite total-degree truncations times $f_i$ converge to $a_if_i$. Closedness of $M$ therefore puts $K=(f_i)$ in $M$; the reverse inclusion holds because a supported sum is a finite sum of series multiples of the $f_i$. Hence $K=M=\ker r$. Apply the Hilbert-dimension conclusion of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] with $I=K$: $H_K=H_D$, and all of $K$ has supported generation. Prefix homogeneous division was already obtained in Step 1; supported generation of $K$ here uses the full family.

source.place: BM 1997, Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5, p.263; the passage from monomial multiplication certificates to the closed supported-sum space is written explicitly here.

proof.text: If $S$ fails, then some $\operatorname{ord}f_i<d_i$: expansion by the distinct $Z$-monomials makes this exactly a failed coefficient inequality. Let $k=\min\{\operatorname{ord}f_i:\operatorname{ord}f_i<d_i\}$, and retain the degree prefix $P=\{h:d_h\le k\}$ with diagram $D_P$. Every retained $f_h$ has order $d_h$; otherwise its order would be less than $d_h\le k$, contradicting minimality of $k$. The proof of Step 1, for this prefix, gives the homogeneous basis and continuous division, even though the later generators may violate $S$. Apply [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] with these divisors and $I=K$, which contains them. Thus $H_K(t)\le H_{D_P}(t)$ for every $t$. Because all omitted vertex degrees exceed $k$, $D_P$ and $D$ agree through degree $k$, so $H_K(t)\le H_D(t)$ for $t\le k$. This includes an empty prefix.

source.place: BM 1997, (7.2)(2) and Corollary 7.4, p.263; agent-written minimal failing order argument for the stronger certificate interface.

proof.text: Choose $i$ with $\operatorname{ord}f_i=k<d_i$ and let $h=\operatorname{in}_k(f_i)\ne0$. If $P$ is nonempty, use its last accumulated essential block $Z^\ell$. A degree-$k$ monomial has $Z^\ell$ exponent $\delta$ of size at most $k<d_i\le Q+1$. For $\delta$ in the restricted prefix diagram the assumed membership $\partial_{Z^\ell}^\delta f_i\in(Z^\ell)$, evaluated at $Z^\ell=0$, reads $\delta!\,[ (Z^\ell)^\delta ]f_i=0$. The coefficient here is a whole series in all complementary variables. Characteristic zero makes $\delta!$ invertible, so every such coefficient vanishes. Thus $h$ is supported outside $D_P$; this is automatic if $P$ is empty. The homogeneous basis from Step 3 implies that this nonzero complement-supported polynomial is independent of the supported degree-$k$ prefix columns. Modulo $\mathfrak m^{k+1}$ those prefix columns have independent lowest homogeneous parts in every degree at most $k$, with total number $\#\{\eta\in D_P:|\eta|\le k\}$. The column $f_i$ supplies one further independent relation: in any dependence, take the smallest total degree; prefix independence eliminates all degrees below $k$, and in degree $k$ the complement-supported $h$ is independent of the remaining prefix columns. Consequently $H_K(k)<H_{D_P}(k)=H_D(k)$. Together with the inequalities through $k$ in Step 3 this proves $H_K<_{\mathrm{lex}}H_D$.

source.place: BM 1997, (7.2)(5), p.262, and the supported-basis dimension count of Corollary 7.4; explicit agent-written strict-drop argument, not an application of the geometric equality-locus theorem.

proof.text: Under $S$, let $e=W_j$. In the unique division $a=\sum q_i(a)f_i+r(a)$ multiply by $e$. All quotient supports remain allowed, and $e\,r(a)$ is still supported outside $D$, because membership in $D$ depends only on the $Z$ exponent. Uniqueness of division therefore gives $r(ea)=e\,r(a)$ and, by induction, $r(e^va)=e^v r(a)$. If $e^va\in K=\ker r$, the latter expression is zero. Multiplication by $e^v$ shifts the $W_j$ coefficients of a formal series injectively, so $r(a)=0$ and $a\in K$. This proves $K:e^\infty=K$, including $v=0$. In general $K\subseteq K:e^\infty$ induces surjections of every truncated quotient, so $H_{K:e^\infty}(t)\le H_K(t)$ pointwise. Hence a strict lexicographic drop from Step 4 cannot be restored by saturation.

source.place: BM 1997, Lemma 7.3 and Lemma 7.5, p.263; coefficient-coordinate saturation proved directly by uniqueness, with no flatness or freeness theorem invoked.

proof.text: In a boundary chart the ordinary pullback is $f_i'=\sum_\gamma\sigma(c_{i\gamma})Z^\gamma$, with $\sigma(W_u)=e$, $\sigma(W_v)=e(\xi+V)$ and $\sigma(Z)=Z$. There is no division by an exceptional power in this assertion. Applying the continuous substitution to a certificate gives $Z^\beta f_i'=\sum_h\sigma(q_h)f_h'$. Since first-vertex supports restrict only $Z$, these new quotients remain supported. Also $\partial_Z^\delta\sigma(f)=\sigma(\partial_Z^\delta f)$ coefficientwise, and the ideals $(Z^\ell)$ are preserved; a local Taylor homomorphism carries the Jacobian units to units. At every model point where the stipulated pure forms and certificates are retained, Steps 1--5 apply to this new series family itself. They give exactly the new coefficient-order test, Hilbert comparison and saturation conclusion asserted. This is a conditional assertion about those model points, not an invariance assertion at arbitrary points of an equality-locus-only basis.

source.place: BM 1997, Theorem 7.21(2), p.269, boundary substitution formula; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 and BMT 2009 section 5.2 for the route. The conditional Taylor-model application is direct substitution.

proof.text: After a coefficient-field embedding $L\hookrightarrow L'$, each finite-degree homogeneous basis remains a basis by [lem-trf-homogeneous-division-extra-variables]. Whole-series identities and derivative memberships map coefficientwise; nonzero coefficients stay nonzero and Jacobian units stay units. A coefficient's order is unchanged because its first nonzero coefficient remains nonzero. Thus the arguments of Steps 1--6, including finite-degree dimension counts, apply over $L'$. If $s=0$, then $K=0$ and $D=\varnothing$; the monomials of degree at most $t$ form the finite basis of $A/\mathfrak m^{t+1}$, giving $H_K=H_D$. All coefficient conditions are empty and coefficient-coordinate multiplication is injective directly. There is then no failure case to minimize. Empty sets of coefficient variables make the saturation assertion vacuous.

source.place: BM 1997, formal supported division in section 7, including the empty family; BMT 2009 sections 6.1--6.2 for coefficient-field and presentation context.

split_report.summary: Seven explicit steps prove the supplied certificate interface using existing extra-variable and continuous formal-division nodes. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q132-79db24a76 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First delivery of Q132 lem-per-hilbert-boundary-supported-certificates: no new nodes, imported statement unchanged, the empty proof replaced by 7 steps; I read all of it. Step 1: under S every term has order >= d_i; vertices are minimal, so 0 is in Delta_i, A_i is nonzero and ord f_i = d_i. The extra-variables lemma (i)=>(ii) with U=W, V=Z, then continuous-formal-division, gives unique continuous division and the closed space M = ker r. Step 2: certificates hold for all Z^beta f_i and W-monomials keep the supports, so closedness gives K = M = ker r and H_K = H_D. Step 3: failure of S means some ord f_i < d_i; take k the least failing order; every generator of the prefix P = {d_h <= k} satisfies S; division of the prefix gives H_K <= H_{D_P}, and H_{D_P} = H_D through degree k. Step 4: the derivative hypothesis (|delta| <= k <= Q) and char 0 put in_k f_i outside D_P, and the minimal-degree independence argument gives H_K(k) < H_D(k), a strict lex drop. This also holds for P empty and k = 0. Step 5: uniqueness of division gives r(ea) = e r(a), so K:e^inf = K; without S saturation only lowers H pointwise. Step 6: the boundary substitution is a continuous local map that keeps every certificate; the clause is conditional and has no e^{-d} division. Step 7: field extension and the empty family are checked. Small cases Z^2+W, Z, Z^2+W^2, the empty family and k=0 all agree. Not a duplicate of lem-trf-coefficient-order-hilbert-equality, coefficient-locus-uniform-division or coordinate-blowup-division-generators (all geometric or controlled-transform statements). ILO VIII 2.3.11-2.3.13 pp.93-94 is only the route reference; BM is not local, so I checked the agent-written proof against the cited node statements.
